items.reason: The rubric review already was a named required check in .github/required-checks.json (merge-gate.mjs enforces its name, PR trigger and non-softening); what was prose is that it blocks on THIS repo's real landing path, since master ships by direct push and the workflow's verdict lands after Vercel starts building — so Part A now runs as the last stage of npm run check:ci (review:agent:gate), which .husky/pre-push runs before any push updating refs/heads/master, test-unit/delivery-contract.test.mjs fails if either wiring is removed, and the review report is kept 90 days as the mechanical-review artifact.

Two of the three findings are false at HEAD and already blocked by scripts/actions-pin.mjs rules P2/P5 (a required check): sast.yml contains no pull_request_target, and every ${{ }} in agent-review.yml is bound in an env: block, never spliced into a run: body. The third is real and I fixed its enforceable half by deleting .github/workflows/ai-review.yml — an Ascent starter scaffold whose only step was `echo TODO`, which had no top-level permissions: block and was therefore failing P1, i.e. `npm run actions:check` and all of check:ci were red on master. SHA-pinning the remaining 21 first-party action refs needs `npm run actions:pin`, which requires network and a shell; this session has neither, and inventing 40-hex SHAs would break every workflow, so STRICT/RATCHET.pinned in scripts/actions-pin.mjs are left as-is for the operator to flip in the same commit that runs the pin.

lessons: In this org's repos, check whether the gap is already enforced before writing anything: systedo-case encodes its own policy as blocking zero-dependency node scripts (scripts/actions-pin.mjs, merge-gate.mjs, sast.mjs) inside `npm run check:ci`, so a generic workflow scanner's 'dangerous pattern' hits here are often false positives that those scripts already block.

Scaffold/starter files dropped into a mature repo can break its gates: the previous autopilot cycle's `.github/workflows/ai-review.yml` (an echo-TODO stub with no permissions: block) violated the repo's own blocking Actions policy and turned a required check red. Before adding a starter, run the repo's gate; prefer extending the real mechanism over placing a stub next to it.

Where a repo ships by direct push to master (Vercel deploys on push), 'required status check on a PR' covers almost nothing — the pre-push hook and the single `check:ci` command are where teeth actually live. Look at how changes land before treating branch protection as the enforcement point.
